skill.name: generating-audio
skill.description: Generates spoken audio from scripts by selecting a suitable model and voice, preparing text for pronunciation, and dividing long material into clips.
skill.summary: Create clear voiceovers, narration, ad reads, and character lines from prepared scripts.
skill.author: supercmohq

security_audit.summary: All 30 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around tool names, parameters, models, and file references. However, the skill contains a high-confidence instruction to rewrite sensitive wording after a safety rejection and retry, which can facilitate moderation circumvention.

remediation.issue: The workflow advises changing sensitive wording and retrying after a safety rejection.
remediation.suggestion: Respect the rejection, explain that the request cannot be generated, and only retry when correcting a clear non-safety technical error.

content.value_statement: Producing natural speech requires careful voice, model, pronunciation, and pacing choices. This skill guides script preparation and consistent text-to-speech generation.
actual_capabilities: Selects an audio model based on expressiveness, duration, cost, and language needs.
Searches available voices using gender, accent, age, language, use case, or descriptive terms.
Presents voice previews before generation when the user has not selected a voice.
Prepares scripts by removing unspoken text and rewriting numbers, dates, currency, acronyms, and URLs for pronunciation.
Splits long scripts into independent clips at natural production boundaries.
Tunes speed, stability, similarity, and style for consistent delivery.
limitations: Generates speech only; it does not create music, sound effects, ambience, dubbing, or voice clones.
Does not mix speech with other tracks or synchronize speech to video.
Requires a configured audio provider and an available voice identifier.
Audio quality and language support depend on the selected model and provider.

use_cases.title: Create Product Voiceovers
use_cases.description: Prepare and generate concise spoken scripts with previewed voices and consistent delivery across scenes.

use_cases.title: Produce Long Narration
use_cases.description: Choose a stable model and divide explainers, documentaries, or chapters into manageable audio clips.

use_cases.title: Generate Character Lines
use_cases.description: Select suitable voices and create alternate takes while preserving each character's voice across lines.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate this script as spoken audio. Show me three suitable voice previews before creating the final file: [script].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a finished script and wants to choose a voice.

prompt_templates.title: Timed Advertisement
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a [duration]-second ad read for [audience], then generate it with an energetic voice after I approve the script.
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer needs a script and audio that fit a fixed duration.

prompt_templates.title: Multilingual Narration
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate this [language] narration using a compatible voice and stable model. Normalize all numbers, dates, acronyms, and URLs: [script].
prompt_templates.scenario: A producer needs clear pronunciation in a supported language.

prompt_templates.title: Directed Multi-Clip Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Split this script by scene, keep one voice and model, tune delivery for [tone], and label every returned clip: [script].
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs production-ready clips with consistent settings.

output_examples.input: Turn this documentary chapter into steady narration without audible changes between sections.
output: A stable narration model and one voice applied throughout.

output_examples.input: Generate two alternate takes of this short character line.
output_examples.output: Two labeled audio takes using the same character voice with controlled delivery variation.

best_practices: Approve the final spoken script and voice preview before generating long or costly audio.
Write numbers, dates, symbols, acronyms, and URLs exactly as listeners should hear them.
Keep the same voice and model across related clips, and split only at real edit points.
anti_patterns: Do not include stage directions, speaker labels, markdown, or delivery instructions in spoken text.
Do not speed up delivery solely to force an oversized script under a duration target.
Do not substitute video generation, music tools, or unrelated speech engines when audio generation fails.

faq.question: Can this skill create music or sound effects?
faq.answer: No. It creates spoken audio only and does not generate music, effects, ambience, or mixed tracks.

faq.question: Does it choose a voice automatically?
faq.answer: It searches suitable voices and normally presents two or three previews for user selection.

faq.question: Can it handle long scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks model limits and splits scripts at natural sections or production edit points.

faq.question: Does it support languages other than English?
faq.answer: Yes, when both the selected voice and audio model support the requested language.

faq.question: Can it clone a voice from a recording?
faq.answer: No. It can use an existing cloned voice identifier, but it cannot create a new clone.

faq.question: What happens when audio generation fails?
faq.answer: It retries ordinary failures once, preserves successful batch items, and reports configuration or voice availability errors.
